tier: RareCloud Residential VPS (Constanta / Navodari) and VPC.KR Korea VPS - Mini

free_tier.stated: No free tier on either. RareCloud's Residential VPS, available only in Constanta (Navodari), was offered as 'Residential VPS - Starting from EUR 11.50/month', 'VPS with genuine residential IP addresses', 'Fully customizable CPU, RAM, storage, and bandwidth', 'Pay only for what you use'. Its store product page answers 'Out of Stock ... orders for it have been suspended until more stock is available' (read on 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-02), and an archived copy of the store listing dated 2026-04-29 shows its box as 'Residential VPS 0 Available', priced from EUR 11.50 monthly; the live listing carries no Residential VPS box. VPC.KR Korea VPS - Mini is $5.80/month: 1 vCPU, 512 MB RAM, 10G NVMe SSD, '5Mbps Dedicated Bandwidth'.
free_tier.notes: The RareCloud store product page for the Residential VPS answers with an Out of Stock notice in place of a plan table ('We are currently out of stock on this item so orders for it have been suspended until more stock is available.'), so no plan row or price can be read from it. The product box, with its stock line and its price, is read from archived copies of the store listing: 'Residential VPS 0 Available', priced from EUR 11.50 monthly, on 2026-02-24 and on 2026-04-29. The live store listing names eight products, none of them a Residential VPS; the starting price is also in the vendor's own offer post. VPC.KR's price is read off its own pricing page.

per_object_cap.notes: The ceiling that matters on this product is stock, not size: the Residential VPS store product page answered Out of Stock on 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-02, and archived copies of the store listing show 0 Available on 2026-02-24 and 2026-04-29.

retention.stated: not applicable: a rented machine and its address, not stored bytes
retention.notes: No retention window on stored objects applies: the product is a VPS with its address ('VPS with genuine residential IP addresses'). What happens to the machine and the address at non-payment is unverified: the offer post states no term for it.

egress.terms: VPC.KR's pricing page states no byte allowance for Korea VPS - Mini: it lists '5Mbps Dedicated Bandwidth' and no overage price, and the vendor's own blog table reads 'Korea VPS - Mini | KT | 5 Mbps | $5.80'. Other VPC.KR pages disagree: two blog posts dated Mar 23, 2026 list '1TB bandwidth' for the Mini beside 1GB RAM and 20GB SSD, a third post of the same date lists 512MB RAM and 10GB SSD and no bandwidth, and the homepage repeats the line '10Gbps Bandwidth' on its Mini, Native SK and AI Agent plan tiles alike, so that line is not a Mini allowance. The order page for the Mini redirects to the login page, so the allowance attached at order time is unverified: behind a sign-up. RareCloud's residential offer says bandwidth is a configuration line the buyer sets: 'Fully customizable CPU, RAM, storage, and bandwidth' and 'Pay only for what you use', with no allowance or overage price stated on the pages read. metered is recorded true because traffic out is a priced configuration line on one product and a hard port rate on the other; no per-byte price is published for either.
egress.free_allowance: unverified: behind a sign-up. VPC.KR's order page for Korea VPS - Mini redirects to its login page, so the allowance attached at order time is not readable. None is stated on VPC.KR's pricing page or in RareCloud's Residential VPS offer; two VPC.KR blog posts dated Mar 23, 2026 list 1TB bandwidth for Korea VPS - Mini, beside 1GB RAM and 20GB SSD that differ from the pricing page's figures for the same plan, and a third post of the same date lists the pricing page's 512MB RAM and 10GB SSD and no bandwidth.

interface_detail: A machine reached over SSH on its fixed IPv4; that shell is the cli token. Orders, renewals and extra addresses go through each vendor's web console (rarecloud.io/clients and console.rarecloud.io; vpc.kr/order and console.vpc.kr). The machine is not a proxy endpoint: SOCKS5, an HTTP proxy or WireGuard is software the user installs on it. RareCloud's offer post says the Linux option lets the buyer 'Configure your own VPNs or create a residential proxy pool with as many additional IPs as you need'.
tooling: An SSH client and a proxy or tunnel daemon the user installs on the machine: SOCKS5, an HTTP proxy or WireGuard. VPC.KR's own setup step for its Korean VPS reads 'Configure WireGuard VPN on your VPC.KR server. This routes your traffic through the Korean native IP while keeping your connection encrypted.' Neither vendor publishes a proxy endpoint, a public API or a wrapper for these machines; the address is the product and the machine is how it is held.
chaining: The Worker opens an outbound connection to the VPS's fixed IPv4 and the VPS makes the upstream request, so the upstream sees an address in AS39347 or AS4766 instead of AS13335. At 45 GB a month across about 599,000 requests the volume is roughly 17 KB/s average, which neither product's published rate comes close to bounding.

limits.value: 5 Mbps dedicated bandwidth on Korea VPS - Mini, the $5.80 tier; the vendor's blog table repeats 'Korea VPS - Mini | KT | 5 Mbps | $5.80'

none published on the RareCloud Residential VPS: bandwidth is a per-order configuration line ('Fully customizable CPU, RAM, storage, and bandwidth') with no stated allowance and no overage price, so this is a documented absence and not a claim of unmetered traffic; the product has no entry in the vendor's public catalog ('Product not found'), so the bandwidth options a buyer could set at order time are unverified: behind a sign-up

limits_note: Four constraints the seven-value vocabulary cannot name. (1) Stock: the RareCloud Residential VPS cannot be ordered. Its store product page answers 'Out of Stock ... orders for it have been suspended until more stock is available' (read on 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-02; an archived copy dated 2026-04-29 answers the same), archived copies of the store listing show its box as 'Residential VPS 0 Available' on 2026-02-24 and 2026-04-29, its landing page redirects permanently to the generic Linux VPS page, and the vendor's public product catalog answers 'Product not found' for it, so the product that passed the registration check cannot be bought. (2) No IPv6 at Constanta: the host rep answered 'Nope. Not yet! We will let you know when it's ready.' to a direct question about IPv6 on RO Constanta, while the datacenter page advertises '14 IPv6 prefixes' and the KVM plan rows list a /112 IPv6 subnet, so the IPv6 in the product table is not IPv6 at this site. (3) One address per machine: the residential offer sells 'as many additional IPs as you need' as a paid option, so a second address is a second purchase, not a rotation. (4) The registration class belongs to the prefix, not to the vendor: the Constanta addresses are announced by AS39347 while the residential test IP's inetnum registrant is 07Internet and the datacenter test IP's is Urban Network Solutions SRL.
binding_note: No limit kind binds: VPC.KR's pricing page gives Korea VPS - Mini a 5 Mbps dedicated port (about 625 KB/s) and states no byte quota, while two VPC.KR blog posts dated Mar 23, 2026 list 1TB bandwidth for the same plan; the monthly volume stated under chaining reaches neither figure. RareCloud states no byte quota for its Residential VPS, and neither vendor publishes a request rate or an object cap. What decides this pair is stock and the registration class of the prefix, and the limit vocabulary has no kind for either.

identity_cost.detail: An email address is the login; RareCloud also requires a phone number. The sign-up form at console.rarecloud.io/register marks these fields required in the served HTML: first name, last name, email, password (at least 8 characters), phone (type tel), street address, city and postcode, with country and billing-currency selects beside them, and the page states '30-second signup. No credit card required to browse.' VPC.KR's register form at console.vpc.kr asks for name, email, password and password confirmation only. Neither form has a card or identity-document field. The structured kind is any-phone, the stricter of the two forms.

reliability_note: Registry class and usage class disagree for the residential test IP 89.33.93.50. A forum member reports its IP2Location usage type as '(DCH) Data Center/Web Hosting/Transit'; a second member's posted IP-intelligence JSON for it lists the asn AS39347 (STYLISH BY A&L SRL, route 89.33.88.0/21) with type isp, the company Orasul Navodari PNV with type hosting, and privacy hosting true. The host rep answers 'ip2location it's not reliable enough' and publishes no corrected reading in the thread.
confidence_note: Documented. The registration of the published test addresses is measured: RIPE RDAP returns inetnum 89.33.92.0 - 89.33.95.255 (SELL-07INTERNET-RO-2, ASSIGNED PA, country RO) for the residential test IP 89.33.93.50, and RIPEstat and APNIC RDAP cover the other two addresses. Prices are documented from the vendors' pages and offer posts, identity from the two sign-up forms as served, stock from the store page's out-of-stock notice. Measured would need the cheapest plan at each vendor, the registry check repeated on a delivered IPv4 rather than a published test address, and a month of byte counts through the machine. The usage-class reading of 89.33.93.50 rests on single IP-intelligence lookups posted on a forum.

evidence.proved: RIPE RDAP: inetnum 89.33.92.0 - 89.33.95.255, netname SELL-07INTERNET-RO-2, type ASSIGNED PA, country RO, maintainers ro-07internet-mnt and SELL-MNT, admin and tech SELL-RIPE, abuse role '0 7 I N T E R N E T . R O - NOC', remarks 'Orasul Navodari PNV' and 'www.07internet.ro'. RIPE stat network-info and prefix-overview: the covering announced prefix is 89.33.88.0/21 and its origin is AS39347. This is the address the vendor publishes as its residential test IP, and its registrant is a local ISP rather than a hosting company.

AS39347 handle SELL-AS, registrant entity ORG-SBAS3-RIPE with fn 'STYLISH BY A&L SRL' and adr 'str culturii, nr 16, 905700, navodari, ROMANIA'; maintainer ro-07internet-1-mnt also appears as a registrant entity. A RIPE search for ORG-SBAS3-RIPE returns org-type LIR, country RO, and its LIR contact address is on the 07internet.ro domain, which ties the announcing AS to the ISP that holds the block.

The second address the vendor publishes, on its datacenter page, is a different registered object from the residential one: RIPE RDAP returns inetnum 85.122.120.0 - 85.122.123.255, netname URBAN-NETWORK-SOLUTIOS, type ASSIGNED PA, country RO, remarks 'Urban Network Solutions SRL, Bd. Mamaia Nord ... Navodari, Constanta', while RIPE stat prefix-overview reports the covering prefix announced by AS39347. Registration and announcing AS are two facts and they do not have to name the same company.

APNIC RDAP: inetnum 112.160.0.0 - 112.191.255.255, netname KORNET, type ALLOCATED PORTABLE, country KR, description 'Korea Telecom', admin and tech IM667-AP, abuse IRT-KRNIC-KR. RIPE stat network-info: AS4766, covering prefix 112.168.0.0/13; prefix-overview names the holder 'KIXS-AS-KR-KR - Korea Telecom' and warns that the queried address is not itself announced, having been aligned to the covering /13. ALLOCATED PORTABLE is the strongest form of the claim: the block was allocated directly to the carrier, not sub-assigned from an upstream.

Korea VPS - Mini: 'Korean Native VPS', $5.80 /mo, 1 vCPU / 512MB RAM, 10G NVMe SSD, '5Mbps Dedicated Bandwidth', feature line 'Korea Local IP'. The $18.99 Native SK tier carries 'Korea Native IP' and '10Gbps Uplink'; the $33 AI Agent tier is the one marked 'Out of Stock' on this render.

The vendor's own plan table: 'Korea VPS - Mini | KT | 5 Mbps | $5.80', 'Korea VPS - Native SK | SK Broadband | 500 Mbps | $18.99', 'Korea VPS - AI Agent | SK Broadband | 500 Mbps | $33.00', with 'All plans include KVM virtualization, NVMe SSD storage, and IPs allocated from primary Korean ISP blocks' and 'Korean native IPs, sourced from local ISPs such as SK Broadband and KT'.

Where 112.169.175.10 comes from: a member publishes it as VPC.KR's test IP with an IP2Location reading of 'ISP - Fixed Line ISP, ISP: KT Corporation, ASN: AS4766 Korea Telecom, Net Speed: DSL, Data Center: No', and adds that KRNIC whois may show the allocation as commercial, which he says is not contradictory because his criterion is the address's usage classification rather than the block's registrant. So the address is a customer's sample, not one the vendor publishes on its own site.

Host-rep offer post: 'We've launched our brand-new Residential VPS, available only in Constanta', 'Fully customizable - CPU, RAM, storage, and IPs', 'Residential Test IP (Constanta, Navodari): 89.33.93.50 <- check it yourself - it's 100% residential', and separately 'Constanta Test IP (Navodari): 85.122.120.20'. Page 2 of the same thread carries the disagreement: a member reports that 89.33.93.50 reads 'Usage Type: (DCH) Data Center/Web Hosting/Transit' in IP2Location, and the host rep replies 'We have tested in a lot of places, and with more tools. ip2location it's not reliable enough. I will get back to you with more details after I talk with my colleague responsible with this product.'

The vendor's own price and terms for the residential product: 'Residential VPS - Starting from EUR 11.50/month', 'VPS with genuine residential IP addresses', 'Fully customizable CPU, RAM, storage, and bandwidth', 'Pay only for what you use'.
The host rep's answer to 'and is IPv6 operational on RO Constanta (Navodari)?': 'Nope. Not yet! We will let you know when it's ready.' That is the source of the no-IPv6 caveat at this site.

The Constanta page labels the location 'AS39347', publishes 'Test IP 85.122.120.20', describes 'RareCloud-operated facility partnered with local residential ISP 07Internet', says the network is 'classified as Eyeball on PeeringDB', and states '14-15 IPv4 prefixes (11,520 IPv4 addresses). 14 IPv6 prefixes'. The IPv6 line is the one the host rep contradicts for this site, and the AS39347 label is the vendor's own claim, which the RDAP check above confirms as the announcing AS.

The sign-up form as served marks these fields required: email, password, phone (type tel, placeholder '[number removed]'), address, city, postcode, with country and billing-currency selects. The page states 'Get started with RareCloud 30-second signup. No credit card required to browse.' No identity document field exists in the form.

The sign-up form carries exactly four inputs: name, email, password, password_confirmation. No phone, no card and no document field appears in the served HTML, which is what makes VPC.KR's identity cost an email.
